items.title: Economic Sustainability as a Factor of Resilience of Economic Systems in the Crisis-Digital Paradigm of Sustainable Development Management
items.abstract: Purpose: To examine the relationship between economic sustainability, innovation, and sustainable development as key determinants of the resilience of modern economic systems and identify strategic approaches for strengthening resilience through digital transformation. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employed a qualitative research design based on a systematic review of scientific literature, comparative analysis, and conceptual synthesis. The review covered 31 studies (2020–2026) retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, supplemented by Google Scholar, and identified the principal mechanisms that enhance the adaptability and long-term stability of economic systems. Research Limitation: The study is conceptual and based on secondary sources. Future research should validate the proposed framework using empirical evidence from different sectors. Findings: The results show that economic sustainability is closely linked to integrating technological and digital innovations into production and management processes. Structural adaptability, system integration, stakeholder participation, human capital development, and effective resource management were identified as key prerequisites for sustainable growth and resilience. Automation, digitalisation, and artificial intelligence improve business processes, increase operational efficiency, and support sustainable development by integrating economic, environmental, and social objectives. Practical Implication: The findings guide policymakers and business leaders in designing innovation-driven strategies that enhance economic resilience. Social Implication: Strengthening economic sustainability promotes long-term stability, social well-being, environmental responsibility, and resilience. Originality/Value: The study integrates the established constructs of economic sustainability, innovation, digital transformation, and resilience into one framework; what is new is the crisis-digital paradigm, which treats digital tools as a system-forming element of resilience management.

items.title: Edukasi AI untuk Siswa Kelas VI Sekolah Dasar Negeri 26 Kota Bengkulu
items.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology makes it important for young learners to become familiar with the basic concepts of artificial intelligence (AI). Many elementary school students use AI-enabled applications in their daily lives, such as voice assistants and content recommendation systems, without necessarily understanding how these technologies work. This community service activity introduced basic AI concepts to 28 Grade VI students at State Elementary School 26, Bengkulu City, on 27 August 2026, through interactive lectures, educational games, question-and-answer sessions, and simple demonstrations. Descriptive observations of student participation during the activities indicated enthusiasm and engagement with examples of AI, its benefits, and its risks. No formal evaluation instrument, pre-test/post-test scores, or numerical outcome measurements were available; therefore, the extent of learning improvement cannot be quantified. The activity provides an initial model for introducing age-appropriate AI literacy in elementary schools.

items.title: Effectiveness of the Working Mind for Managers Program With People Leaders in a Transportation Organization
items.abstract: Workplace mental health challenges are prevalent in high-demand, male-dominated industries such as transportation, where job design, safety risk, and cultural norms may discourage help-seeking behaviors. However, limited evidence exists on whether workplace mental health training leads to sustained outcomes in real-world organizational settings. Leadership-focused mental health training has demonstrated improvements in stigma reduction and resilience, yet few studies examine whether these effects are sustained beyond the immediate post-training period. This evaluation examined the 6-month outcomes of The Working Mind for Managers, a manager-focused mental health training program, within a large Canadian transportation company. Data were collected between June 2022 and August 2024. Using a repeated-measures design, matched pre-training and 6-month follow-up survey data were analyzed to assess mental health stigma, resilience, confidence to address workplace mental health issues, and self-care practices. Results indicated sustained reductions in mental health stigma, with the strongest changes observed in workplace-relevant domains, including work-related beliefs/competency and perceptions of responsibility. Managers demonstrated significant improvements in resilience and confidence, along with modest increases in self-care practices. Findings are interpreted within social cognitive and adult learning frameworks, alongside organizational and implementation perspectives, highlighting the role of leadership capacity in sustaining workplace mental health training. These results contribute to the limited evidence on long-term outcomes and provide practice-relevant insights for implementing and sustaining manager-focused mental health training in real-world workplace settings.

items.title: Effects of Cueing and Self-Explanation on Chemistry Video Learning Across Tasks with Different Cognitive Demands
items.abstract: Abstract Video-based instruction can support students’ understanding of abstract chemical concepts, but its effectiveness depends largely on the use of appropriate instructional strategies. This study examined the effects of cueing and self-explanation on chemistry video learning in terms of learning performance, intrinsic motivation, cognitive load, and visual attention. To examine whether these effects differed across chemistry learning tasks with different cognitive demands, two experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 employed a concept-knowing task, whereas Experiment 2 employed a knowledge-application task. A total of 60 grade 10 students were randomly assigned to one of the two experiments. Each experiment used a 3 (no cue, color-based cue, or contour-based cue) × 2 (with or without self-explanation) between-subjects factorial design. Fixation duration and fixation count were used to assess visual attention. Subjective workload was assessed using a self-report questionnaire, with pupil diameter providing additional evidence related to cognitive effort. The findings showed that cueing significantly affected learning performance, visual attention (fixation duration and fixation count), and pupil diameter, but no significant differences were found between the two cueing types. Self-explanation significantly improved learning performance, intrinsic motivation, and visual attention. The effects of cueing and self-explanation did not differ significantly between the two learning tasks. These findings suggest that chemistry educators can integrate cueing and self-explanation into video-based instruction to support both conceptual understanding and knowledge application.

items.title: Electronic Health Record User-driven Evaluations and Adaptations of Large Language Models for Clinical Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are emerging as generalist tools capable of interpreting clinical language and supporting healthcare professionals across diverse medical contexts and tasks, making electronic health records (EHRs) a natural and powerful setting for their deployment. Yet realizing this potential safely and effectively in real-world practice requires solutions adapted to EHR users' needs and context. To propose a new paradigm for medical LLM development and evaluation that places EHR users, data, and EHR infrastructure at its center. In this narrative review, we propose three mutually reinforcing pillars of the EHR ecosystem: the daily users of these systems, such as physicians and nurses; the rich and detailed EHR data produced through routine clinical care; and the EHR system as institutional and technical infrastructure. We then examine the role these pillars play in LLM development and evaluation. We show that daily EHR users provide essential input for aligning LLMs with real clinical needs; EHR data offer the most meaningful foundation for model alignment and assessment; and the EHR system as infrastructure shapes what effective and responsible deployment looks like. Together, these pillars are shown to play an essential role in developing trustworthy and useful LLMs adapted to clinical applications, conducting reliable and meaningful evaluations, and assessing the impact of LLMs in real healthcare settings. A paradigm centered on EHR users, data, and systems is needed to develop, evaluate, and deploy LLMs that are trustworthy, useful, and adapted to real-world clinical practice.

items.title: Elevating English Proficiency via ChatGPT-Assisted Learning in Tourism and Hospitality Education: Unpacking the Roles of Self-Regulated Learning and Intrinsic Motivation
items.abstract: This study investigates the association between ChatGPT use for learning and Tourism English proficiency among hospitality and tourism students at Egyptian public universities, examining self-regulated learning (SRL) and intrinsic motivation (SIM) as mediating mechanisms. A quantitative cross-sectional design was adopted, with online survey data collected from 795 students across nine public universities. All participants reported using ChatGPT for English-language learning. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed to assess the measurement and structural models, including construct reliability, validity, and common method bias. The results indicate that ChatGPT use is positively associated with perceived communicative proficiency in Tourism English, SRL, and intrinsic motivation. Both SRL and SIM partially mediate the relationship between ChatGPT use and perceived communicative proficiency. These findings underscore the potential of generative AI to support autonomous learning and intrinsic motivation in Tourism English education. However, proficiency was self-reported and therefore reflects perceived rather than objectively demonstrated competence.

items.title: Embodied Inclusion in Emotionally Aware Hybrid Learning Environments: A Case Study on Visual Impairment
items.abstract: The diffusion of digital technologies and artificial intelligence has transformed contemporary learning ecologies, reshaping the embodied, relational, and affective configurations through which participation and belonging are constructed. Hybrid learning environments increasingly emerge as spaces where physical and digital dimensions, technological mediation, communicative practices, and affective processes interact (Floridi, 2014). Within this framework, inclusion cannot be reduced to technological access; it must be understood as the co-construction of participation by bodies, technologies, and interactions. This perspective aligns with embodied cognition approaches (Gallagher, 2005) and sociocultural perspectives that emphasize the mediational nature of learning (Vygotsky, 1978). In contexts involving students with visual impairments, accessibility and relational belonging are deeply interconnected (Pérez-Pereira & Conti-Ramsden, 1999). Emotionally aware learning environments should therefore be understood not merely as systems that detect emotional states but as relational ecologies that sustain affective attunement and shared participation (Stern, 1985). items.title: Emerging Technologies and Assessment Innovation in European Online Higher Education
items.abstract: Digital assessment has become a strategic component of online higher education, supporting not only the certification of learning outcomes but also feedback processes, student monitoring and quality assurance (JISC, 2020). Recent technological developments have expanded the possibilities of assessment through Artificial Intelligence (AI), learning analytics and immersive technologies, which are increasingly associated with personalised feedback, adaptive assessment, data-informed decision making and authentic learning experiences (Holmes et al., 2023; Kamalov et al., 2023). While the educational potential of these technologies has been widely discussed, less attention has been devoted to their institutional formalisation. Technological innovation does not automatically translate into institutional adoption. Universities may experiment with innovative tools without integrating them into policies, governance structures, assessment strategies or quality assurance systems. For this reason, understanding how emerging technologies are represented within institutional documentation can provide valuable insights into the maturity of digital assessment ecosystems. items.title: Empowering Women through AI: Ensuring Safety and Awareness
items.abstract: Women face multiple challenges in achieving financial independence and personal safety. Although digital solutions exist, entrepreneurship guidance and emergency safety mechanisms are often provided separately. Women interested in starting businesses may lack structured information about startup opportunities, investment requirements, essential skills, financial assistance, and implementation procedures. Personal safety also remains a concern during travel, education, employment, and daily activities. This paper proposes ShaktiSafe, an integrated mobile application designed to address both challenges through a unified platform. The system consists of a Women Empowerment Module and a Women Safety Module. The empowerment module provides categorized business ideas, estimated investments, required qualifications, essential resources, and step-by-step implementation guidance. The safety module incorporates SOS alerts, voice-activated assistance, live location sharing, and emergency contact management. Artificial intelligence can support business discovery and information access, while mobile computing, database management, and location-based services enable essential functions. Multilingual interaction and an accessible interface are considered to support users with different levels of digital literacy. By integrating economic guidance with personal safety features, ShaktiSafe aims to promote awareness, entrepreneurial participation, confidence, and financial independence.

items.title: Engagement of Older Adults with AI-Supported Healthcare Systems and the Risks of Age-Based Exclusion
items.abstract: This article argues that older adults’ engagement with healthcare systems supported by artificial intelligence (AI) cannot be explained solely by access to technology or individual levels of digital literacy. The central claim is that when older adults are unable to benefit fully from these systems, the problem is often framed as a personal failure to adapt, whereas the deeper issue is a form of sociotechnical exclusion produced at the intersection of data representation, design norms, limited explainability, inadequate institutional support, and age-based bias. To explore this issue, the article draws on a composite case involving an older woman who struggles to use an AI-supported chronic disease monitoring application. It first examines the opportunities associated with artificial intelligence in the care of older adults and the conceptual tensions surrounding these technologies. It then presents the composite case and analyses it through the lenses of digital exclusion, digital ageism, participatory design, care ethics, and nursing practice. The article concludes that the success of artificial intelligence in healthcare should be assessed not only in terms of accuracy, speed, and efficiency, but also in terms of its capacity to involve older adults in care processes in ways that are understandable, safe, fair, and dignified.
